conversations.evidence: Earlier Python implementation passed the official 20 public cases and the protocol handshake.

conversations.student: The student asked me to inspect the official repository and web page and granted computer control.
conversations.agent: I found oceanbase/seekdb's 2026-competition-round2 branch containing STDIO_PROTOCOL.md, mysqltest (20 public cases), and protocol_check. This replaced the earlier guessed MySQL wire protocol with JSON Lines.
conversations.evidence: Official branch files: STDIO_PROTOCOL.md, mysqltest/manifest.json, protocol_check/run.py.

conversations.student: The student provided a reference Rust implementation commit and asked me to study it and reach equivalent capability.
conversations.agent: I studied the reference architecture: framed WAL with CRC and completion markers, disk-backed row/index storage, compact float32 vector codec, external merge sort for wide rows, bounded-memory TopK, and exact/ann both executing exact search. I replaced the Python prototype with a Rust engine following the same design, kept the JSONL protocol and the learning material, and added the reference legacy test kit.
conversations.evidence: Commit replaced minivectordb/*.py with src/*.rs, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, and a scratch-based multi-stage Dockerfile.

experiments.purpose: Run the official 20 public cases through the Rust Docker image.
experiments.output: 20/20 PASS (sql_*, storage_*, transaction_*, vector_*); RESULT PASS.
experiments.interpretation: The Rust engine satisfies the public functional assertions including BIGINT, Unicode, float32 storage, filtered TopK, ties, transactions and restart.

experiments.purpose: Run the reference legacy test kit (three hidden-risk cases).
experiments.output: legacy_filtered_topk PASS; legacy_index_rollback_restart PASS; legacy_failed_index_tx PASS; RESULT PASS.
experiments.interpretation: Filtered TopK, index maintenance across rollback/restart, and atomic failed multi-row insert inside an explicit transaction all behave correctly.

experiments.purpose: Verify the Docker image handshake and shutdown.
experiments.interpretation: The process emits exactly {"type":"ready"}, answers shutdown, and exits zero.

experiments.command: tools/verify_extended.py --scenario large|wide|crash|oracle (requires a Linux cgroup v2 host)
experiments.output: Tooling is ported but not executed under cgroup v2 in this run.
experiments.interpretation: The Rust engine implements the mechanisms these scenarios target (framed WAL, disk index, external sort, bounded TopK) but the cgroup-bounded scenarios were not run on the CI runner.

student_evidence: The student supplied the complete task screenshots and the official reference commit, and repeatedly required verification rather than unsupported claims.
The student granted computer control for the repository/web inspection that located the official public package.
The student directed the study of a reference implementation and asked for equivalent capability, driving the Python-to-Rust replacement.
result_evidence: GitHub Actions round2-official-check run 43608849255: handshake PASS, 20/20 public PASS, 3/3 legacy PASS.

The submitted tree contains src/*.rs (protocol, sql, types, engine, storage, disk_index, query, distance, hot, half, vector_codec, read_batch), Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock and a scratch multi-stage Dockerfile.
retrospective: The earlier MySQL-wire guess was wrong; the official JSONL protocol fixed the framing.
The reference commit demonstrated that the hidden risk is bounded memory: wide rows and larger-than-memory tables. Its legacy test kit captured exactly those behaviors.
A compiled Rust engine removes the Python object/JSON overhead that dominated large-table writes and wide-row sorting.
limitations: The cgroup-bounded large/wide/crash scenarios were not executed on the CI runner.
ann mode still performs exact search rather than an approximate index, which keeps recall at 1.0 but is not a performance-optimal ANN.
Formal hidden cases are not public; passing 20 public + 3 legacy does not guarantee all 29 formal cases.
